findings.reason: citing the two existing run-directory message surfaces would force the design to state whether the inbox extends one of them or genuinely needs a third, which is the decision §7 currently leaves open.
findings.text: §4 proposes "a coordinator writes a message into the run's own directory; the worker's prompt contract obliges it to read that directory at checkpoints" and §7 names only "the prompt-composing module" and "the CLI module", citing neither `reckon/crew/resumption.py:809` (which already writes a coordinator instruction, `resume-<turn>-advice.txt`, into the run directory and hands it to the worker) nor the durable per-run peer channel at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3026` (`_channel_root` → `run_dir(run_id)/peer-channel`) exposed through `peer_ask`/`peer_read` with the PEER CHANNEL prompt block at `reckon/crew/prompts.py:619`. A plan adding a subsystem over machinery it never searched is a finding, and the plan's own recorded comment at line 244 already concluded "the existing peer-channel block is the one place the contract already does a blocking directory read, so the inbox should reuse it" — a conclusion the design section does not carry.

findings.reason: requiring the justification would either delete the wrapper in favour of extending the peer channel or record the concrete property (mid-turn read at a checkpoint) that the existing machinery cannot supply, which the plan now asserts without stating.
findings.text: the §7 inbox is a second reader/writer over the same per-run directory the peer channel (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3026`) and resumption advice (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:809`) already use, and the plan gives no reason those cannot be extended — e.g. admit the coordinator as a channel sender, or add a one-way "instruction" kind beside the peer channel's "question" — so the honest change is an extension of an existing mechanism, not a parallel channel.

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the author extend one durable per-run channel (adding a coordinator-sender and an instruction kind) rather than shipping a forked mailbox that drifts from the peer channel's durability and NEEDS-HELP semantics.
findings.text: the plan re-implements per-run-directory message placement and delivery instead of extending the owner: `reckon/crew/resumption.py` (`_write_resume_prompt`, `resume-<turn>-advice.txt`, the existing coordinator-writes-into-the-run-directory path) and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (`_channel_root`, `_write_json`, `peer_ask`, `peer_read`, the existing durable per-run message channel), with the worker-side read contract owned by the PEER CHANNEL block in `reckon/crew/prompts.py:619`.

findings.reason: §4's own done-when requires that an unread inbox be distinguishable from silence, which cannot be specified without one module owning the mailbox record and its read/receipt state.
findings.text: the inbox has no owning module: the write side is "the CLI module" (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py`) and the read side is the prompt-contract in `reckon/crew/prompts.py`, so the mailbox shape, the at-checkpoint read obligation and the "unread inbox must be visible" rule from §4's done-when are spread across two files with no interface naming what a message is, where it is stored, or how a worker tells "no message" from "message not yet read".

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — no module owns the inbox; the design splits it into a prompt-contract obligation in `reckon/crew/prompts.py` and a coordinator-side writer in "the CLI module" (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py`), leaving the mailbox's shape, delivery contract and unread-visibility rule spread across two files with no single owner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements per-run-directory message placement and delivery rather than extending the owner, which is `reckon/crew/resumption.py` for the run-directory advice write and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (`_channel_root`, `peer_ask`, `peer_read`) for the durable per-run channel.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's live design (§4 inbox + §7) proposes a new coordinator→worker message channel in the run directory without citing the two existing mechanisms it most resembles: the run-directory advice file written by `reckon/crew/resumption.py` and the durable per-run peer channel in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` with its PEER CHANNEL prompt block in `reckon/crew/prompts.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the coordinator-side writer is a thin layer over the run directory and the plan never says why the existing run-directory write path or the peer channel cannot be extended instead.
